source.title: Just how goal-directed are hippocampal theta sweeps, anyway?

confidence_rationale: Deliberately sought out as the non-degeneracy / skeptical counterweight to the Yu et al. and Tang et al. entries in this directory (per this repo's standing lit-pull discipline, e.g. SD-097's own inclusion of Kinny & Georgeff 1991 as a skeptical baseline). Author credentials are strong (A.D. Redish is a senior, long-standing figure in hippocampal decision-making/vicarious-trial-and-error research) and the framing -- 'a simpler mechanism, fundamentally incompatible with those planning hypotheses' -- is a real, named alternative account, not a vague caveat. Confidence held LOW because the full text could not be accessed: nature.com redirects to an authentication wall (idp.nature.com) and no open-access mirror was found. This entry rests entirely on WebSearch-surfaced paraphrase, corroborated across two independent searches but never the primary text itself.
failure_signatures: Full text inaccessible (Nature paywall; no PMC/bioRxiv mirror found for a commentary/News & Views piece, which typically are not deposited as preprints). The specific 'simpler mechanism' this commentary proposes as an alternative to planning-grounded interpretation was NOT identified in this pull -- only that one exists and is described as 'fundamentally incompatible' with the planning hypotheses MECH-236/MECH-289 lean on.

Cannot rule out that this commentary's skepticism is narrowly scoped to a specific claim in Yu et al./Tang et al. (e.g. a particular statistical inference) rather than a wholesale rejection of goal-directed theta-sweep interpretation in general -- without the full text this entry cannot distinguish 'the whole framing is contested' from 'one specific analytical step is contested.'

mapping.source_claim_statement: Per WebSearch-surfaced paraphrase (full text not accessed): planning is thought to be grounded in hippocampal sequences, but recent studies have suggested a simpler mechanism -- described as fundamentally incompatible with those planning hypotheses -- may underlie these sequences. The Yu et al. and Tang et al. papers in the same issue are characterised as first steps toward resolving this controversy, not a resolution of it.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the skeptical counterweight to the supports-direction entries in this directory. If the 'simpler mechanism' this commentary names turns out to explain theta-sweep goal-direction WITHOUT requiring anything like MECH-236's goal-conditioned trajectory generation or MECH-289's generative sweep, that would weaken (not falsify) the biological-precedent case for those claims' specific mechanistic framing -- though it would not touch REE's own architectural motivation for having SOME destination-privileging and generative-traversal mechanism, which does not depend on the biology being resolved either way.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Included specifically as a non-degeneracy check on the other three entries in this directory, per this repo's lit-pull discipline -- NOT as a claim this commentary directly evidences a specific REE mechanism. The entry's own low confidence reflects that its content is known only at one remove (search-engine paraphrase of a paywalled commentary), which is a materially weaker evidentiary basis than the other three entries in this directory.
mapping.source_context: Nature Neuroscience News & Views / commentary accompanying the Yu et al. and Tang et al. empirical papers in the same 2026 issue; not a primary data source.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality moderate: reputable venue and credentialed author (Redish), but a commentary/News & Views piece is inherently lower evidentiary weight than a primary empirical paper, and this entry could not verify beyond search-engine paraphrase. Mapping fidelity low because the specific competing mechanism was never identified, only its existence and stated incompatibility with planning-style interpretation.
